activity.notes: Varkhuman was the Sogdian king/Ikhshid based at Samarkand, not ruler of a single centralized state encompassing every Sogdian principality. Chinese sources recognized him as governor of Samarkand and Sogdiana between 650 and 655 and formally invested him in 658; the conventional reign reconstruction extends to about 670. ATLAS therefore uses Samarkand (Sogdiana) and approximate endpoints.

sources.title: AFRĀSIĀB ii. Wall Paintings — Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.citation_text: Iranica identifies Varkhuman in the Afrasiab inscriptions as sovereign and records Chinese recognition of him as governor of Samarkand and Sogdiana in 650-655 and official investiture in 658.

sources.title: SAMARQAND i. HISTORY AND ARCHAEOLOGY — Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.citation_text: Iranica states that the famous Samarkand wall paintings were commissioned around 660, probably by King Varkhuman himself.

sources.title: Life and Worldview of the Sogdians according to the Afrasyab Paintings
sources.citation_text: The scholarly article places Varkhuman as king of Samarkand around 650-675 and ties the Afrasiab inscriptions and murals to his court.
